detailed_rationale: India Glycols is an unusually diversified chemicals company spanning bulk/specialty/performance chemicals, natural gums, potable spirits, industrial gases, sugar, nutraceuticals, and bio-fuels/ethanol blending. The ethanol-blending business ties into India's multi-year government-mandated ethanol-blending program, a genuine structural tailwind alongside the potable-spirits business. FY26 (Mar 2026) sales were Rs.4,211cr (+12% YoY) with net profit of Rs.293cr (+27% YoY) -- profit outgrowing revenue, a healthy margin-expansion signal (Screener.in). Q4 FY26 revenue actually declined ~5% YoY but profit still rose 34%, again pointing to margin/mix improvement rather than demand weakness. Debt (~Rs.1,691cr) and interest coverage (~3.9x) are moderate, not alarming, though not as strong as the better-capitalized names in this batch.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold on both windows. Fundamentals here look reasonably healthy -- growing profit, real segment diversification, and a structural ethanol-blending tailwind -- with nothing rising to the level of a genuine Hold-vs-Sell tension, so Hold stands without escalation.
summary: India Glycols is a diversified chemicals and spirits business benefiting from India's ethanol-blending push, with profit growing faster than revenue in recent periods on improving margins. We rate this a Hold.
positive_para: The business spans genuinely complementary segments (specialty chemicals, spirits, ethanol) with a structural tailwind from India's ethanol-blending mandate, and recent results show profit consistently outpacing revenue growth -- FY26 profit up 27% against 12% sales growth -- a sign of improving operating leverage.
negative_para: Revenue growth itself is unspectacular in the most recent quarter (down ~5% YoY) and the business remains a diversified conglomerate of moderately-related segments rather than a focused compounder, with interest coverage (~3.9x) that is only moderate rather than a clear strength.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~26x earnings with ROE/ROCE in the 11-12% range, the valuation is neither obviously cheap nor stretched -- it is consistent with a diversified mid-cap chemicals business with a genuine but modest structural growth driver (ethanol blending) rather than a high-conviction re-rating candidate.
